orders.reason: Pancytopenia and splenomegaly with weight loss

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Came for BP but the real story: since around January more tired than he's ever been, naps afternoons. Fills up after half a plate, belt is looser. Wife thinks he's lost weight; scale here confirms, 92-93 all of last year, 88.5 today. No fevers or sweats he's noticed. No bleeding, no black stools. Cough at baseline. Leg better since the infusion.

Exam: tired-appearing but comfortable. Conjunctivae a little pale. No lymphadenopathy neck, axillae, groin. Abdomen: spleen edge firm and palpable well below the left costal margin, nontender. Liver not enlarged. Lungs with a few wheezes, his usual. No edema, no petechiae.

CBC this afternoon: Hgb 9.2, WBC 2.6, plt 84. All three lines low, which is new (CBC normal in 9/2021).

A/P
1. Fatigue, early satiety, weight loss with an enlarged spleen and low counts in all three lines. Needs hematology quickly. Urgent referral placed, called their office myself, they will see him 4/24. Reviewed with pt and wife by phone this afternoon; bleeding and fever precautions.
2. HTN, CKD 2: BP as charted. BMP today. No changes.
RTC after heme.

events.reason: Pancytopenia, splenomegaly, fatigue and weight loss

reports.text:
Specimen: bone marrow, right posterior iliac crest, aspirate attempt and trephine core.
Aspirate: no particles obtained (dry tap); touch preparations of the core made instead.
Core: 1.6 cm adequate core. Marrow largely replaced by fibrosis, with clusters of atypical megakaryocytes showing hyperchromatic, cloud-like nuclei. Reduced erythroid and granulocytic elements. Reticulin and trichrome stains confirm increased fibrosis. Dilated sinusoids with intrasinusoidal hematopoiesis. No increase in blasts by CD34. No metastatic carcinoma.
Molecular studies sent separately.
reports.conclusion: Bone marrow: fibrotic myeloproliferative neoplasm, consistent with primary myelofibrosis in the appropriate clinical setting.

documents.title: Hematology-Oncology Consultation
documents.author: hematology-oncology
documents.body:
Outside hematology-oncology clinic
Date of consultation: 04/24/2023 (letter includes results through 05/01)
Patient: Bernard Bennett, DOB 07/03/1955

Dear colleague,
Thank you for the urgent referral. Mr. Bennett is 67 and comes with his wife. Over three months he has grown steadily more tired, feels full after small meals, and has lost weight without trying. You found low counts and a large spleen on 4/11.

Background: hypertension, no prior cancer. Chronic bronchitis and Paget disease of the left tibia (zoledronic acid 12/2022). CKD, BPH, urethral stricture, lumbar spondylosis. Former smoker, 40 pack-years. Meds: hydrochlorothiazide, lisinopril, tamsulosin, vitamin D, acetaminophen PRN. NKDA.

Exam: pale, no jaundice. Marked splenomegaly reaching well below the left costal margin. No lymphadenopathy. No hepatomegaly.

Labs today: hemoglobin 9.0 g/dL, WBC 2,500/uL, platelets 80,000/uL. Smear reviewed personally: many teardrop red cells, occasional nucleated red cells and immature granulocytes (leukoerythroblastic picture). No circulating blasts of note.

Bone marrow 4/24: the aspirate was a dry tap, so a trephine core was taken in the same sitting. Pathology (5/1): marrow fibrosis with clustered atypical megakaryocytes, consistent with primary myelofibrosis. JAK2 V617F detected. Abdominal ultrasound 4/27: spleen 19 cm, liver normal in size.

Impression: JAK2-positive primary myelofibrosis with symptomatic splenomegaly, constitutional symptoms and cytopenias.

Plan: We discussed the nature of this disease with him and his wife. Given his age and other conditions he is not a candidate for stem cell transplant and we will focus on symptom control. I will see him on 5/10 to start a JAK inhibitor and go over its monitoring. We will do his blood counts here every few weeks at first, then about every three months.

With thanks,
Hematology-oncology

reports.text:
Indication: splenomegaly.
The spleen is enlarged, measuring 19 cm in craniocaudal length, with homogeneous echotexture and no focal lesion. Liver normal in size and echotexture, no focal lesion. Gallbladder without stones. Common bile duct not dilated. Kidneys normal in size without hydronephrosis. Pancreas partially obscured by bowel gas. No ascites.
reports.conclusion: Splenomegaly, 19 cm. Liver normal in size.

documents.title: Hematology Follow-up
documents.author: hematology-oncology
documents.body:
Hematology follow-up 05/10/2023, Mr. Bennett, primary myelofibrosis.
Symptoms unchanged: tired, early fullness. Counts similar to 4/24.
With platelets in the 80s, starting ruxolitinib at 5 mg twice daily. Reviewed common effects: lower blood counts, especially anemia early on, dizziness, bruising, infections including shingles (he has had both Shingrix doses), weight gain, raised cholesterol. Avoid starting strong CYP3A4 inhibitors without checking with us.
Through the specialty pharmacy. CBC in 4 weeks, visit in 3 months.
Current medications per patient: HCTZ 25, lisinopril 10, tamsulosin 0.4, vitamin D 1,000 units, acetaminophen as needed, now ruxolitinib 5 mg BID. NKDA.
Hematology-oncology

documents.title: Specialty pharmacy notice
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Specialty pharmacy faxed confirmation: Part D prior authorization for ruxolitinib approved through 5/2024, prescriber hematology. Copay assistance through a foundation being arranged by heme's office. First fill shipping 5/17. Added to med list as outside prescription. FYI to PCP.

documents.title: New pill
documents.author: patient
documents.body: The blood doctor started me on Jakafi. Is it ok with my blood pressure pills? My wife wants to know if I should still take the vitamin D. Thanks, Bernard

documents.title: RE: New pill
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Bernard, yes, ruxolitinib is fine alongside your blood pressure pills, tamsulosin and vitamin D. Keep everything as is. Before you take any new medicine, including antibiotics or antifungals someone else prescribes, ask them to check it against ruxolitinib or call us. I'll keep up with hematology's letters. Hang in there.

documents.title: Hematology Follow-up
documents.author: hematology-oncology
documents.body:
Myelofibrosis follow-up, 08/09/2023.
Three months on ruxolitinib 5 mg BID. Energy noticeably better; early fullness gone; regaining weight, now 90 kg. No bleeding, no infections.
Exam: spleen smaller, edge now palpable below the costal margin but softer and less far down.
CBC today: counts steady to slightly improved from diagnosis.
Plan: continue ruxolitinib 5 mg BID. CBC and visit in 3 months. Allergies: NKDA.
Hematology-oncology

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Wellness visit, a calmer year than the spring.
- Myelofibrosis: on ruxolitinib via hematology, feels better, eating normally, weight back up. Counts and spleen followed there.
- Paget: leg pain mostly gone.
- Cough: same winter pattern, no blood.
- Function: independent, still driving, small carpentry jobs. No falls. PHQ-2 1 (a little down in the spring, better now).
- Memory: no concerns raised today.
- Advance directive reviewed, unchanged.

Exam: vitals as charted. Spleen tip palpable. Lungs few wheezes. Heart regular. No edema.

Plan: BMP, UACR, lipids, A1c, PSA (CBC at heme). Flu, updated COVID and RSV at a nurse visit in October. Lung CT November. Colonoscopy due next year, will talk then given his platelets. RTC 6 mo.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Inactivated vaccines only (on ruxolitinib; heme ok'd these). HD flu L, updated COVID R, RSV L lower. Firm pressure 2 min each site given platelets; no bruising before leaving.

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
reports.text:
Indication: Annual lung cancer screening. Former smoker, 40 pack-years.
Comparison: 11/17/2022.
Findings: New 3 mm solid nodule, right upper lobe. No other nodules. No consolidation. No effusion. Heart and mediastinum unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Lung-RADS 2: 3 mm solid right upper lobe nodule, benign appearance or behavior. Continue annual screening in 12 months.

documents.author: hematology-oncology
documents.body:
Seen 11/20/2023 for primary myelofibrosis on ruxolitinib 5 mg twice daily.
Doing well. Good appetite, active, no night sweats. Spleen tip about 4 cm below the left costal margin today.
CBC stable: anemia and thrombocytopenia unchanged, no transfusion need.
Continue current dose. Return 3 months with CBC.
NKDA. Hematology-oncology
